content.text: I reviewed the full package — brief, disclosure, every USER passage in the conversation, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs — and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 20 claims (independent claims 1, 11, 16 and dependent claims 2-10, 12-15, 17-20) were traced limitation by limitation to the disclosure: rigid base with first/second sides, vibration motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter member (plastic, metal, PTFE, combination of rigid materials) at the perimeter of the second side terminating in a bearing face, deliberate non-seal with a clearance admitting ambient air, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, resulting pressure differential holding the device without operator downforce, an all-rigid vibration transmission path free of elastomer/foam/resilient mount, sliding to successive areas while the hold is maintained, handles for guiding, and a rope/wire/cable flexible pulling element giving decoupled control. Claims 10 and 15 (stirring elements) and the FIG. 6 autonomous-movement embodiment trace to the affirmative USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"; the Field's "moving autonomously" traces to the same passage. All 17 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes exactly one part across the numeral table, the description, the Brief Description of the Drawings and every figure brief, each appears in at least one brief, and each brief's numeral list matches its identification list. Section-line designations were verified as the same repeated designation in all three places: line 2-2 appears in the FIG. 2 view line, the FIG. 3 brief (numeral 2 at both ends, arrows), the Brief Description and the detailed description; line 4-4 likewise. FIG. 2 (bearing places) and FIG. 4 (clearance place) are mutually consistent with the "along at least part of the perimeter member" recital, and the recently repaired FIG. 2 entry in the Brief Description now matches the FIG. 2 brief's cut bodies (slab, legs, band). Cross-checks of claims against description found identical relationships and terms with clean antecedent basis; the abstract is 145 words; cross-reference and government-support sections follow the brief; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, or unresolved alternative remains in any application section. Generic outlines (rectangular slab, band, ring, blocks, cord) are confined to the briefs, marked schematic, and matched by shape-neutral claims and description, with no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening leaking into the application text. Two defects were found and are reported: a self-negating disclaimer in the FIG. 2 brief that directs a through-slab flow passage and then states no passage structure is asserted, and an untraced material-property phrase ("hard and dimensionally stable") in the detailed description where the sources support only rigidity. Everything else in the ledger is supported and internally consistent.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief directs a flow passage through the base and then denies that any passage is asserted
findings.where: figures/FIG-2-VERTICAL-SECTION-THROUGH-THE-CHAMBER.md, "Geometry to be drawn", final sentence of the second paragraph
findings.detail: The brief instructs the renderer to draw a passage that penetrates the base from the inside of the air-extraction housing to the chamber, and then closes with a disclaimer that denies the very feature just directed. Directing a body and then denying it is the same instruct-then-deny defect that was previously repaired in the FIG. 6 stirring-element paragraph, and it leaves the authoritative brief self-contradictory: a renderer cannot both draw the through-slab gap and assert no passage. The depicted communication itself is source-supported and should stay, because the disclosure affirmatively places the extraction mechanism on the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side; only the overshooting half of the disclaimer is untrue of the sheet. The disclaimer can truthfully cover the width, the position along the slab, and the absence of any particular port, duct or valve construction, none of which the sources give, but it cannot truthfully say no passage is shown. No application text is affected: the detailed description and the Brief Description of the Drawings say only that the air-extraction mechanism 20 is coupled to the first side 14 and is in fluid communication with the chamber 22, so the convention is otherwise properly confined to the brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG. 2 brief): "A plain unhatched gap interrupts the hatching of the slab beneath the housing and runs through the slab from the inside of the housing to the chamber 22, so that the air-extraction mechanism 20 reads as being in fluid communication with the chamber 22; the gap is schematic, its width and position along the slab being a convention for this sheet only, no port, duct, valve or other passage structure being asserted." Supporting source for the depicted relationship (disclosure.md): "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base." The disclosure gives no width, position, or construction for any passage, which is what the disclaimer may properly cover.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2-VERTICAL-SECTION-THROUGH-THE-CHAMBER.md, replace the clause "no port, duct, valve or other passage structure being asserted" with "no particular port, duct or valve construction being asserted", so the sentence reads: "A plain unhatched gap interrupts the hatching of the slab beneath the housing and runs through the slab from the inside of the housing to the chamber 22, so that the air-extraction mechanism 20 reads as being in fluid communication with the chamber 22; the gap is schematic, its width, its position along the slab and its drawn form being a convention for this sheet only, no particular port, duct or valve construction being asserted." Change nothing else in the brief and no application text.

findings.title: Detailed description attributes hardness and dimensional stability to the perimeter member, which the sources do not disclose
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "The perimeter member and the chamber", last sentence of the paragraph beginning "The perimeter member 24 is not a seal."
findings.detail: The sentence asserts two material properties of the perimeter member, hardness and dimensional stability, neither of which appears in the disclosure or in any affirmative USER passage. The sources characterize the perimeter only as rigid, as made from plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, as not relying on flexible rubber or foam, and as maintaining rigid contact with the tile. Hardness is a distinct property from rigidity and is not implied by the disclosed material list (PTFE in particular is not a hard material), and dimensional stability is a further untraced characterization. The contrast the paragraph draws, a conforming compliant cup against a non-conforming rigid member, is fully carried by the disclosed word "rigid", so the untraced properties can be removed without losing any supported substance. No claim recites hardness or dimensional stability, so the fix does not disturb claim-to-description consistency.
findings.evidence: Candidate (08-detailed-description.md): "The perimeter member 24 is instead hard and dimensionally stable, and it makes rigid contact with the exposed face 38." Nearest source passage, which supports rigidity and rigid contact but says nothing about hardness or dimensional stability (disclosure.md): "Unlike conventional vacuum grippers or suction cups, the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam. Instead, it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile." No affirmative passage in the disclosure or in any USER message describes the perimeter member as hard or as dimensionally stable.
findings.fix: Amend the sentence to read: "The perimeter member 24 is instead rigid and does not conform to the exposed face 38, and it makes rigid contact with the exposed face 38." Leave the rest of the paragraph, the claims and the numeral table unchanged.
